# Bar-Persistence Census — scalp viability (GENERATED by backtest.bar_persistence)

Terms: [docs/GLOSSARY.md](../../docs/GLOSSARY.md).

Engine `8effbb323` — OBSERVATIONAL, pre-registered (prereg_bar_persistence, register 63). **MEASUREMENT FOR SCALP-VIABILITY ASSESSMENT, NOT A STRATEGY: any scalp recipe is a separate counted registration, gated on cells that clear spread AND baseline and survive forward accrual.** Entry = next 1M open after fire; horizons N in {1,3,5,10} settled bars; reach cells print gross/NET-of-spread percentages (the net column is the scalp economics); the points ladder is HOME-REFERENCE ONLY, the ATR ladder cross-instrument. Floors: each signal's headline cell reads against its matched baseline ensemble median [range] — random entries also see favorable bars. ° = n<20. Full signal×session×horizon×threshold grid in the JSON.

**PER-BAR EXPECTANCY CURVE (register 64):** signed points at the close of bar+k, k ∈ {1…10}, cumulative and incremental, gross and net (spread charged once at entry). PURPOSE: peak-k and the incremental sign-flip bar are the mechanical inputs a scalp recipe's TIME-EXIT would cite; the reach columns are what a TARGET-BASED recipe (resting order at the level; touch = fill, queue-risk optimism stated) would cite. THE TWO COLUMNS NOMINATE DIFFERENT HARVEST MECHANICS BY CONSTRUCTION (register 64 amendment): wick-based reach pays a resting order, close-based expectancy pays a time-exit — recipes cite which column they live on. No recipe registers without its question grading YES (Q2-H6, register 64). The md prints cumulative net medians at k ∈ {1,3,5,10} and peak-k; full curves in the JSON. **FILL MODELS (register 65): this page renders BOTH families — the reach columns are touch=fill (OPTIMISTIC); the expectancy columns are close-based; the harvest ladder (SIGNAL_POINTS) is stop-fill PESSIMISTIC. The families are NOT COMPARABLE; recipes cite which column they live on.**
